implement: legion-worker: the phase contract, the PR body template and what a proof on a production-like surface is
dispatch: the surfaces changed are Dispatch's own (approval requests, decision-block answers, the request-approval command) and its 'Approval of a spec' text is being rewritten
ce-simplify-code: the simplify pass over the settled server (docs/approval_carry.go, docs/approval_review.go) and web (EarlierApproval, decision-blocks) code before the handoff
test: legion-worker: the tester drives the changed surface for real and records its proof as references/pr-body.md defines
dispatch: to drive a real Dispatch through its API and commands and read a document's approval state
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md and references/review-threads.md for the review round
thermonuclear-deep-review: a server rule that writes an approval in a human's name is a correctness and trust boundary
dispatch: the skill text under review is this skill's own rule

findings.finding: docs cannot call api.writeReview or closeAskTx (api imports docs); the carry has no writer of reviews or closer of the open approval ask in the package writeVersionTx lives in.
findings.answer: Plan 2.4: review writing moves to docs (docs.WriteReview, one writer; api's two callers delegate), canonicalLogin moves to model.CanonicalLogin, the carry lives in docs/approval_carry.go and answers an open request itself; the event owner mirrors ownerForArtifact (IssueKey for an issue document, ArtifactID for a project document).

findings.finding: Claim that whole-document uploads are written outside writeVersionTx is unsupported; a human upload differing only inside blocks would carry.
findings.answer: Checked: uploads write their row in api/artifacts.go:288-308 (writeDocumentVersion) and issue_create.go:329-332, outside writeVersionTx, as the spec says. Plan 2.1 also makes the trigger a newly answered block in the tree, so no answer-less version carries whatever its text.

findings.finding: writeVersionTx has neither the previous version nor the answerer's identity; the detector's inputs are unspecified.
findings.answer: Plan 2.1-2.2: the previous version and the approved version are read from artifact_versions in the transaction; answers are read from the trees' server-owned attributes (answered_by, answered_at); the answerer is never the version's actor. Server test: the answer settles in one version with an unrelated in-block agent edit.

findings.finding: A re-answered block is not a 'first answer', yet the spec promises the carry for a re-decided decision.
findings.answer: Plan 2.1: newly answered means the new tree holds an answered block the previous tree lacks or holds with a different answered_at, so a changed answer carries; a server test covers the replace-answer path (expected_answer_at).

findings.finding: Blocks that never get an answer (resolved, deleted, withheld) have no reading in 'every block added since has his answer'.
findings.answer: Plan 2.2.4-2.2.5: an open or resolved block added since his approval stops the carry (the spec's literal stale case); a block of the approved version that is gone stops it too (the added guard, section 8); withheld answers leave the attributes unset, so no carry. One server test per state.

findings.finding: Three review queries hide behind two sentences; whether another human's changes_requested blocks the carry is unsaid; two humans answering in one version is unsaid.
findings.answer: Plan 2.2.1-2.2.2 and 2.1: his latest review (any state) must be approved; no changes_requested by anyone newer than it; the card reads the latest approved row whoever wrote it; when newly answered blocks name two humans nothing carries. Server tests per case.

findings.finding: The carried review's actor has no full-fidelity source: answered_by is an id string, reviews store a model.Actor.
findings.answer: Plan 2.2.1: match answered_by to his latest approved review by CanonicalLogin and reuse that row's actor JSON verbatim; the server test asserts byte equality.

findings.finding: Copies of an ask on other documents also get a version that first holds his answer.
findings.answer: Plan 2.1: blocks carrying copied_from are ignored, so the carry fires only on the ask's own document; a server test uses a copied block on a second approved document.

findings.finding: artifact.approved sequences before artifact.version inside the transaction, and the contract's documentation knows only two provenances of an approval.
findings.answer: Plan 2.3 and task 7: the order is harmless to the daemon (ApplyDesignGateEvent) and asserted by a server test (both in one commit, the approval's seq lower); the contracts comment, packages/envoy/AGENTS.md and the route docs name the carried provenance (ask_id null, reason names the carry).

findings.finding: The open approval request is moved by MoveApprovalAsk and then must be closed by the carry; order and mechanism are unsaid.
findings.answer: Plan 2.3: move first (the request names the version the review pins, the invariant api/reviews.go:324-331 keeps), then answer it in his name with Approve and the carry sentence, ask.answered appended, its id on the review; a server test covers it.

findings.finding: Stage 3 cannot hold two READY-gated cycles in one merging stint, so the spec's proof sequence is unimplementable as written.
findings.answer: Plan 3.5 and departure 1: the single READY cycle goes to the carry; the outside-the-blocks edit is proven by gate state before it (closed, no review, no artifact.approved) and reopened by the human's header approval; the jq negative control stays.

findings.finding: Stage 3 mechanics the spec hides: inserting the block as an agent, finding the ask id, answering with expected_edited_at, the waits.
findings.answer: Plan 3.5 tasks 19-20: dispatch_agent helper (bearer plus session actor), the edits route insert, the poll of GET issues/{key}/asks?state=open for the block ask, the human answer with expected_edited_at null, and each wait.

findings.finding: 'No review the human wrote' cannot be checked, since the carried review's actor is the human.
findings.answer: Plan 3.5 step 3: machine checks instead - approvedVersion == currentVersion at the answer's version, the newest review's version, actor, null ask_id and reason, no approval ask opened at the carry, the artifact.approved event present, and no reviews-route write by the script in that window.

findings.finding: Where the card's earlier-approval fields live, whether a move refreshes them, and rows written before the change.
findings.answer: Plan 2.4-2.5: three optional fields on model.AskApproval and the contracts AskApproval, filled at openApprovalAsk from the latest approved row; no refresh needed because every later approval closes the open request; absent fields render as a first request (covered by the web test).

findings.finding: The card's date format and timezone are unspecified and the mandated web test depends on them.
findings.answer: Plan 2.5: the UTC calendar date of approved_at (YYYY-MM-DD) in a <time> element carrying the full instant, the approver through actorLabel; the web test asserts the exact line.

findings.finding: Cutting decision blocks is defined once and written twice (Go tree, browser lines); nested blocks use longer fences; 'the blank line it owns' names no side.
findings.answer: Plan 2.5: the cut is defined (fence of N>=3 colons closed by exactly N after the same prefix, plus the blank line after the closing fence, or before the opening one at the document's end); both tests read the same three fixtures under packages/contracts/fixtures/decision-blocks/.

findings.finding: Acceptance bullet 3 (skills and prompts) is prose about a live architect; only the file text is checkable.
findings.answer: Plan 3.3-3.4 and acceptance entry 5: the pinned envoy-client test and the prompt tests are updated and run, the grep sweep over the named files lists only rewrite-branch sentences, and the one-sentence summary and no-new-wave rules are review-checked as the spec says.

findings.finding: 'An architect's edit inside a block does not stale' is false once an answer has carried: a later in-block edit closes the gate.
findings.answer: Plan 2.2 (last paragraph) and 2.6: no answer-less version carries; the skills say the gate closes at such a version and reopens at the answer, and that an in-block edit before the answer does not prevent the carry.

findings.finding: Production Dispatch must run the change; the spec's proofs run elsewhere, and the deployment's deploy role was unverified by the analyst.
findings.answer: Plan section 7: the deployment instructions name the dispatch-deploy role; the implementer publishes the merge commit to it, waits for /healthz, then drives a scratch LEGSMOKE document with two human clicks asked through one dispatch ask; the architect decides whether that ask is acceptable.

findings.finding: Claims checked and found supported: writeVersionTx is the one version path and moves the open request; the daemon opens the gate on artifact.approved regardless of order and reads no actor; the header approval closes an open request; the browser has a pure two-version diff.
findings.answer: Relied on in plan 2.3, 2.4 and 2.5 with the same citations.

specDepartures.spec: Stage 3 bullet: after the human approves the root spec the driver adds a decision block, the merger's READY is refused at that version, the human answers the block and the issue reaches awaiting_merge on the carried artifact.approved; the negative control stays the existing check, an edit outside the blocks keeping READY refused until the human approves.
specDepartures.plan: One READY refusal/release cycle in the issue: it goes to the carry (block inserted, READY refused at its version, answer carries, awaiting_merge). The outside-the-blocks upload runs before it as a gate-state check: the gate closes, no review and no artifact.approved are written, and the human's header approval reopens it; the existing jq negative control stays on the refusal's state file.
specDepartures.evidence: A READY refused while the gate is closed is held and accepted at the first reopen, moving the issue to awaiting_merge (packages/daemon/internal/workflow/ready.go:208-259; the script's own comment at scripts/e2e/stage3-devbox-workflow.sh:801-802), so a second refusal has no merger in merging left to refuse.

acceptance: The stage 3 bullet's negative control: an edit that changes text outside the blocks closes the gate and writes no review and no artifact.approved; the human's approval reopens it. The READY refusal and its release by the carry are proven once, at the decision block's version.

specDepartures.spec: The comparison cuts every decision block out of both versions and requires every block added since the approved version to have his answer; it says nothing about a block of the approved version that is no longer there.
specDepartures.plan: The carry also requires every decision block of the approved version to be present in the new version (by block id); a removed block stales as a text change would.
specDepartures.evidence: With blocks cut out whole, a version from which an agent deleted an answered decision block compares equal to the approved one, so the answer that follows would approve the deletion unread, which the spec's own principle forbids ('letting it carry would approve an agent's edit of the Acceptance unread').

specDepartures.spec: The comparison names only the blocks added since the approved version as the ones that must carry his answer; a block the approved version already held is outside its words.
specDepartures.plan: Condition 2.2.4 tests every decision block of the new version that is not as the approved version held it (added since, answered or re-answered since by anyone, or resolved since) and requires it to be his answer; a block answered before his approval and untouched since is content he approved and stays out. Decided by the architect on the first testing round (Envoy e492cea1f11ad15f80fc1bbe15091432, confirmed 3d4a59f1d75d041455b6c81d828b0655); plan.md version 2 records it as departure 3.
specDepartures.evidence: The tester's PROOF-14: a second human answered a block the approved version held open after the approval, then the approver answered a block the agent added, and the literal rule carried his approval over the other person's decision unread, against the spec's own principle that his answer carries his approval only when it is the whole change.
